context:
Goal: your plain "use Opus" message lifts the model cap with no override words (your pick at 19:47 CST).
Problem (risk): the third review found the build lets text you did not type grant Opus to every role for 2 hours. A message that starts a new session, or a scheduled reminder, counts as your turn, and the judge said yes to 3 of 10 Claude-written texts. The cause: the override code counts `/effort` command records as your turns. The change is parked until you decide.
Based on (measured): third review of the build, at its latest commit 2954de20 (21:56 CST).
Based on (ruling): roles-review-cap-three: a change held after its third review waits for your word.
Departs from: main, where Opus is lifted only by `opus 2h` or `override` — your plain ask also lifts it.

options.gain: The plain ask ships with no hole.
options.how: A fix lane makes the override code count only messages you typed, not session starts, reminders or command records. Then one fresh review.
options.label: Fix the hole, then one more review
options.lose: One more lane before it works.

options.how: The batch runner merges the build now.
options.label: Merge as it is
options.lose: A new session's first message or a reminder can raise every role to Opus for 2 hours.

options.how: The lane closes; main keeps the keyword forms only.
options.label: Drop it
options.lose: You keep typing `opus 2h` when your plain words already said it.

title: Your plain "use Opus" message: fix the hole first, merge as it is, or drop it?
why: Recommended: a. The plain ask still ships, without letting non-owner text raise every role to Opus.
